name: Hooks
note: Your scripts run on agent lifecycle events
summary: The harness runs user-defined commands at fixed points in the agent loop, such as before or after a tool call, when a prompt is submitted, or when a session starts or stops. A hook can log, add context or block an action, so a rule is enforced by code instead of being left to the model.
how: Register a command for an event such as PreToolUse in a settings or hooks.json file
When the event fires, the harness passes the event as JSON on stdin
The hook's exit code or JSON output allows, blocks or annotates the action
Plugins can bundle hooks so they install together with skills and MCP servers
facts: Claude Code, Codex, Claude Cowork (hooks from plugins)
PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, SubagentStart, Stop, SessionStart
Shell commands; Claude Code also supports HTTP, prompt and agent hooks
Deterministic control, but every hook is code that runs on each matching event
goodFor: Blocking dangerous commands before they run
Formatting, linting or logging after every edit
Organisation-wide policy that the model can't skip
watchOut: A hook from an untrusted repo or plugin runs code on your machine
Slow hooks add latency to every matching tool call
